title: Decoupled ingress/egress floor with sampled stream‑metering and grace tier
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: current hosted API billing conflates ingress and egress tokens into a single floor model that penalizes small bursty customers and creates awkward unit economics on streaming. Teams ask for predictable minimums while also wanting fair treatment for low-traffic customers and enterprise customers onboarding with SQ/contract credits.

Proposal summary: introduce a decoupled ingress (input) vs egress (output) floor where: (1) microtier floors apply for very low-volume customers (<X tokens/day) for each direction independently; (2) streaming sessions are metered using a sampled stream‑metering algorithm (sample N% of streaming tokens for floor accounting) to avoid per-request overhead and to allow a reduced streaming floor; (3) an onboarding grace tier grants temporary credits and a 30‑day graduated floor ramp for enterprise SQ/onboarding flows.

Goals: reduce friction for low-volume devs, avoid large floor subsidies for bursty low-margin workloads, preserve predictable baseline revenue for hosting, and make enterprise contract crediting explicit and traceable for sales/finance.

Key design decisions to validate: decoupled floors by direction, sampled streaming for floor attribution, grace-tier crediting with time-based decay, and retaining existing per-token unit prices unchanged for now.
experiment_design: Cohort A: control (current unified IO floor). Cohort B: decoupled microtiers only. Cohort C: decoupled microtiers + sampled streaming floor at 10% sampling rate. Cohort D: Cohort C + 30‑day onboarding grace credits for enterprise SQ customers. Randomize new signups and a stratified sample of existing eligible active customers. Run for 8 weeks with interim checks at weeks 2 and 4. Implement server-side flagging and telemetry. Use holdbacks for risk mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: net-revenue_change >= -2% (expected short-term dip) with revenue recouped by month 3
no increase in latency or SLO violations attributable to metering
support ticket volume for billing <= +15% vs baseline
enterprise SQ onboarding time reduced by >= 20% for pilot accounts using grace-tier
rollout_plan: 1) Implement billing prototype in sandbox with sampled stream-metering logic and flags (Eng). 2) Finance simulations and commit limits (Fin). 3) Legal + Security confirm contract language and SQ flow for credits. 4) Internal dogfood by SE and small customer cohort for 2 weeks. 5) Alpha cohort (2k accounts), measure. 6) Broader beta (10k accounts) with guardrails and rollback paths. 7) Full rollout with sunset plan for legacy floor if metric gates pass.
risks_mitigation: Risk: sampled metering undercounts streaming heavy workloads -> Mitigate: conservative sampling (start 10%), validate against full-accounting logs, provide per-account auditing window. Risk: confusion in billing statements -> Mitigate: add per-invoice line items and explanatory tooling in console. Risk: revenue loss -> Mitigate: dynamic floor thresholds and temporary opt-in paid beta for high-risk customers.
implementation_notes: Engineering to expose two new meter tags (io_direction: ingress|egress) and a sampled_stream flag. Billing backfill job required for cohort splits. Console needs UI to show decoupled microtier usage and grace credit balance. Finance to provide synthetic forecast model by March 7. Legal to provide addendum text for SQ credits by March 10.

2025-02-19 Marco Gomez: Engineering feasibility check - sampled streaming is doable but requires a lightweight sampling hook in the runtime; will add spike (ENG-81233) to estimate CPU cost.

2025-02-21 Priya Shen (Finance): Ran initial revenue simulations. If microtier floor set at $1/month per direction, expected short-term revenue dip ~1.5% but increases developer conversion. Requested sensitivity bands and ARR impact table (sheet link below).

2025-02-24 Nora Li (Legal): Enterprise addendum for grace credits needs clear expiry language and auditability. Suggest include 'credit balance' in invoices and a clause for credit recoup on contract termination.
2025-02-27 Eng spike update: sampling hook prototype completed; estimated 0.4% CPU on avg for high throughput hosts. Need one week to wire into billing pipeline for test cohort.

2025-03-03 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and set due_date. Flagged security_review_required. Created GitHub draft PR for billing logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1426
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight sampled counter exported to billing with deterministic seeding to ensure reproducibility. Add test fixture to verify sampled vs full counts. Expose logs for per-account audit for the sampling windows.
notes_for_sales_customer_success: Playbook: explain microtiers as developer-friendly floors that reduce entry friction; show invoice breakdown and grace credit expiration. Sales to offer opt-in for customers that want guaranteed legacy floor behavior during contract negotiation.
qa_checks: Simulate billing for 10k synthetic accounts across typical traffic shapes (botty bursts, steady chat, streaming long sessions). Verify floor attribution and invoice generation. Validate sampled stream accounting against ground truth for 1% of events.
